Unfortunately, House Republican leaders are pushing to gut the GAO by 25% at a time when the public – as well as Democrats and Republicans in Congress – have mounting concerns about the conduct of the Administration – from unauthorized wars abroad to self-administered slush funds.

Yesterday, the House Appropriations Committee debated the Fiscal Year 2027 Energy and Water Development and Related Agencies funding bill. While it did a good job supporting Army Corps of Engineers projects which help many communities with vital waterways and flood mitigation, its shortcomings outweigh its positive elements.

It cuts programs that help us diversify our energy supply chain and make sure that America stays on the cutting edge of research and development, it undermines nuclear security, and it abandons communities dealing with nuclear contamination from past defense projects. As a result, American families and businesses are going to face higher fuel and utility costs and many communities will be left less safe.

During the debate, I tried to improve the bill by supporting an amendment that would increase the critical minerals and energy innovation fund and restore the electricity account. This would help make America more energy independent, maintain the electrical grid and help make sure it is reliable, and ensure that we are not relying on foreign adversaries for materials vital to manufacturing and technology that drive our economy.

The amendment would help make sure that American families can afford to keep the lights on, farmers can operate, and local businesses can continue to function.

You can also watch my opening remarks here:

Dan Marino came to Capitol Hill today to advocate for the Protect College Sports Act.

College sports shaped his life. Now he’s helping lead the fight to protect them from transfer chaos, endless lawsuits, and an unsustainable status quo.

College sports are being pulled apart by transfer chaos, constant litigation, shady NIL deals, disappearing rivalries, and a broken system that is leaving student athletes, schools, and fans without clear rules or real protections.

- Ends the roster chaos with national rules for transfers (one free undergrad) and eligibility (5-in-5)

- Protects student athletes’ right to earn from their own NIL
- Enables enforcement of House settlement on revenue sharing and fake NIL deals

- Protects women’s sports, Olympic sports, and scholarship opportunities
- Preserves historic rivalries
- Keeps college sports tied to education, so student athletes become successful adults
- Prohibits football coaches from quitting mid-season to be hired by another program
- Guarantees safety standards, health care, and an ombudsman for student athletes
- Makes TV money work for college sports with an option for schools to pool media rights
- Stops Super League consolidation

College sports are worth saving.

My amendment to fully fund the Chemical Safety Board was just adopted in committee!

This independent watchdog agency is going to be an important partner in getting answers for the families, loved ones, and community about the catastrophe in Longview.

I sincerely thank my bipartisan colleagues for bucking attempts to eliminate this watchdog agency, and standing for transparency as our community looks for answers.

The horrifying loss of life in Longview last week demands a thorough impartial investigation conducted by the independent watchdog Chemical Safety Board. 

Unfortunately the presidents proposed budget has zeroed out the CSB budget. 

Next week, I’ll be making it my priority to ensure the agency is funded and, in the longer term, work to ensure the board includes the trades experience necessary for a full picture of the complex interaction between lab experience and trades experience.

It’s the lives, land and livelihoods of millworkers at risk here, and I’m here to make sure their voices are guiding the investigation into what needs to be done to rebuild safe and secure jobs, where workers come home to their families at the end of the day.

My gratitude goes to the Longview Fire Department and all the first responders who arrived at the Nippon Dynawave Packaging Company this morning to respond to the explosion.

My heart go out to the families of those killed and injured by this terrible blast. These families will need our help and support in the months and years ahead. If you pray, now is a good time to send up some prayers for the millworkers in Longview and their families.

I am deeply saddened to hear of the death of Sir Alex Younger.

Alex dedicated his life to the service of our country. We are safer today as a country because of Alex’s work.

He was one of the clearest and most thoughtful voices on the challenges facing Britain and the wider world.

I had the privilege of working with Alex at multiple points in my career. Alex was always a source of wise counsel. He took issues, but never himself, seriously. He battled illness with remarkable good cheer and determination.

My thoughts are with his wife Sarah, his family and all those who had the honour of being his friend.

May he rest in peace.

WORLD_FRANCE_PRESIDENT.text:
Bienvenue, cher @magyarpeterMP. 

C’est une nouvelle ère qui s’ouvre en Hongrie, mais aussi pour la Hongrie en Europe !
    
Nous décidons aujourd’hui de lancer la préparation d’un nouveau partenariat stratégique entre la Hongrie et la France, à signer d’ici la fin de l’année. 

Il permettra d’approfondir nos relations dans des secteurs stratégiques comme la défense, l’énergie nucléaire, les infrastructures, les transports ou encore l’agriculture. 

Il contribuera également à notre agenda de souveraineté européenne, capable d’agir pour sa sécurité et sa défense, de renforcer sa compétitivité et de protéger sa démocratie.

À Edgar Morin.
L’hommage de la Nation.

Ce mémorial en hommage aux victimes du génocide perpétré contre les Tutsi au Rwanda est un lieu vivant. Il cultive la mémoire et projette vers l'avenir la relation entre le Rwanda et la France.

À nous de transmettre avec rigueur, dignité, vérité et justice.

Twibuke Twiyubaka.
